title: SMiLE-seq: Selective Microfluidics-based Ligand Enrichment followed by sequencing
protocol: Place molds into a TMCS vapor chamber.
Mix 30g Base with 6g curing agent in a clean plastic cup, maintaining a 5:1 ratio.
Mix the solution for 1 minute at 2200 rpm and degas for 2 minutes at 2400 rpm using a TINKER mixer.
Pour the mixture onto the control layer mold and place it in the vacuum chamber.
Mix 10g Base with 0.5g curing agent in a clean plastic cup, maintaining a 20:1 ratio.
Mix this solution for 1 minute at 2200 rpm and degas for 2 minutes using a TINKER mixer.
Spin coat onto flow layer at 2400 rpm for 35 seconds with a ramp time of 15 seconds.
Remove the control layer mold from the vacuum chamber, ensuring no bubbles remain on the surface.
Place both the control and flow layers in an 80°C convection oven and incubate for 30 minutes.
Remove casts from the oven, cut out the control layer, punch holes, and align to the flow layer.
Put the aligned device back into the 80°C oven and incubate for at least 90 minutes.
Remove devices from the oven and punch holes in a flow layer with a puncher of 2.5-4 mm diameter.
Bond PDMS chips to glass slides and use within the following 10 to 30 minutes.
Incubate plasmid DNA and nuclease-free ddH2O mixture at 25°C for 3 hours or longer.
Mix 5 μl NEBuffer 2, 5 μl dNTPs, 0.5 μl Cy5 labeling primer (500 uM), 1.5 μl library oligos (200 uM), and 37 μl ddH2O.
Incubate the mixture at 94°C for 5 minutes.
Incubate the mixture at 50°C for 60 seconds.
Place tubes on ice.
Add 1 ul of Klenow 3' – 5' exo- to the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 60 minutes.
Keep the mixture at 0°C.
Purify the obtained double-stranded libraries using MinElute and elute in 12 μl of EB.
Dilute the purified libraries 1:10 in ddH2O.
Add 50 ng of poly-dIdC to each 10 μl of diluted libraries.
Mix 2 μL expressed non-purified TF with 2 μL diluted dsDNA library and 2 μL partner TF if applicable.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min or up to 180 min for KRAB ZFPs.
Move the inverted microscope close to the WAGO automated set-up.
Place the clean freshly assembled microfluidic chip on the microscope table.
Connect the control tubing C1 to C11 to the chip as shown in Figure 1B.
Set the operational control pressure of control tubing lines to ~12 psi using pressure gauges.
Open CoDeSyS software and load the custom “SMiLE-automated” script.
Go to “PLC_Visu” tab.
Optional: Use WebVisu mobile (WAGO Corp.) application for remote set-up control.
Plug the tubes pre-filled with BSA-biotin, PBS, Neutravidin, and anti-eGFP antibody to Inlets F1, F2, F3, and F4 respectively as shown in Figure 1B.
Activate the CoDeSys script using Online -> Connect and then Online -> Run.
Start the chip processing by pressing the “Chip Priming” button on the “PLC_Visu” control panel.
Pipette the content of individual PCR tubes into individual chip wells of the sample collectors.
Press the red “Load samples” button to activate on-chip sample loading by capillary force.
When the “Elute” button jumps to red, mix 20 μL of TE with 3 μL of Proteinase K and load in a tygon tube at Inlet 1.
Plug an empty tygon tube as DNA collection tube to Outlet 2.
Press the “Elute” button and wait 30 min.
Collect the TF-bound DNA from the tube plugged to Outlet 2.
Amplify the recovered DNA using HiFi KAPA polymerase.
For the PCR mix, use 10 μL of 5xHF KAPA buffer, 1.5 μL of dNTPs, 0.5 μL of primer GA2seq FW (10uM), 0.5 μL of primer GA2seq RV (10uM), and 0.5 μL of KAPA HiFi polymerase.
Add eluted DNA to the PCR mix and top up with ddH2O for a total volume of 50 μL.
PCR amplify the DNA using a 2 min 95°C hot start followed by 17 cycles (98°C for 20 sec, 65°C for 15 sec, and 72°C for 90 sec) and 2 min at 72°C.
Purify the PCR product using a MinElute kit from QIAGEN.
Elute the DNA in 10 μL of EB.
Sequence the pooled libraries on a HiSeq or NextSeq500 instrument (Illumina) as 2-4% spike-ins to a sequencing lane loaded with other DNA libraries containing compatible Illumina adapters.
Demultiplex and trim raw Illumina reads to 30 bp corresponding to the randomized DNA region using FASTX-tools.
Count identical reads, collapse them into one, and order according to occurrence from most to least abundant (using FASTX-tools).
Identify consensus binding sequences (seeds) through MEME motif discovery.
Use non-collapsed reads to calculate read statistic.
Perform PWM training using HMM as described below.
Define the initial parameters.
Use a MEME-derived seed in IUPAC format.
Modify the seed by adding 1 extra 'N' on each side to allow for a more flexible motif search using the HMM-based program.
Set the read length to 30 bp.
Filter and randomly shuffle the input fasta file to remove 'N' containing sequences, sequences larger than the expected read length, and multiple instances of a sequence.
Execute fa2filtered.pl with parameters for read_length and fasta_file.
Pipe the output from fa2filtered.pl to filtered2unique.pl.
Create an HMM and train it on a subset of randomly selected sequences using mamot.
Estimate the nucleotide background distribution using bc.pl.
Add 1 background nucleotide on each side of the sequences.
Convert 'U' to 'T' characters in RNA sequences and remove non-DNA characters.
Reformat sequences into a MAMOT usable format.
Select between 10,000 and 25,000 sequences for training.
Use the command: ./padseq.pl < left_flank > < right_flank > < bckg > < filtered_fasta_file > | head -n < n_seq > > < seq_file >
Set < left_flank > to "1".
Set < right_flank > to "1".
Define < bckg > with comma-separated background probabilities of each base, e.g., '0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25'.
Specify < filtered_fasta_file > as the input file.
Define < n_seq > between 10'000 and 25'000 for sequence sampling.
Specify < seq_file > as the output file.
